clue.text: Detect in deep sound

definitions.meaning: to find them out or see through them
a low rolling noise, like distant thunder

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a low noise from the depths.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: informally to discover a deception, and a low continuous resonant noise.

clue.text: What's different about this vessel?

parts.note: the question points to the one letter that sets this craft apart from an ordinary boat, the letter standing for undersea

explanation.walkthrough: The vessel is a boat with a single-letter prefix; that letter, and the fact it travels underwater, is what is different about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine of the world wars, named from Unterseeboot, undersea boat.

clue.text: Master a new Latin dance

parts.note: a boss is a master or employer
nova is the Latin word for new (feminine form)

explanation.surface: A teacher shows off a fresh dance from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin dance' looks like one phrase, but 'Latin' goes with 'new' to give the Latin word NOVA, leaving 'dance' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance and musical style blending samba and jazz.

clue.text: Old officer such as Beverley put on staff

definitions.meaning: The rank was the lowest commissioned infantry officer of old
a flag hoisted on a pole

explanation.surface: A former officer named Beverley is given a post on the general staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Beverley is the false identity of Captain Absolute in Sheridan's comedy The Rivals, who poses as a poor junior officer. 'Staff' means a flagpole, not personnel.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank was once the most junior commissioned infantry officer, and the word also names a flag flown from a pole.

clue.text: Train, in infancy, to give blows

definitions.meaning: nursery word for a railway engine, from its puffs of steam
to blow repeatedly, as a smoker or a steam engine does

explanation.surface: Children are trained to hit one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Small children call a steam locomotive by its puffing noise, and the doubled verb means breathing out in short bursts.

clue.text: Stop Patrick on autumn trip

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so these words fall over into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Patrick halts his journey in the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' looks like a journey, but it is the anagram signal on PATRICK ON AUTUMN.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is one kind of symbol used in writing to separate sentences and clauses.

clue.text: Acting as cover, perhaps, for novelist

definitions.meaning: cover is a ... position in cricket, so a player there is out in the field

explanation.surface: Someone stands in for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, cover (or cover point) is a fielding position on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopping the ball in cricket away from the bat is the cricketing sense, and Henry Fielding was the eighteenth-century author of Tom Jones.

clue.text: Point that's crucial to big cheese coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a big cheese is a VIP, a very important person

explanation.surface: An important person arrives at the key moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A central point on which something turns, hence the crucial factor.

clue.text: Copy bills I'm to put in collection of records

indicators.note: the words to put in mean these letters go inside the collection

parts.note: a file is a set of records
A/Cs, accounts, are bills
I'm written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone duplicates invoices to add to the paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: An exact reproduction of a document, as sent by fax.

clue.text: Sound judgment bringing better profit?

definitions.meaning: a better is one who bets, and knowing about horses would make a punter money

explanation.surface: Good sense brings bigger returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as more good, but it is one who bets on horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical common sense, and literally a knowledge of horses that pays off at the racecourse.

clue.text: No such defect in sister on probation

definitions.text: No such defect in sister on probation

parts.words: No such defect in sister on probation
parts.note: a trainee nun is NO followed by a word for a moral failing, so she is literally 'no' plus that failing

explanation.walkthrough: A sister on probation is a NOVICE; split it as NO VICE and she has no such defect.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral failing or bad habit is a vice, which the novice literally has none of.

clue.text: Neat conclusion, of course

definitions.meaning: the final stretch of a racecourse

explanation.surface: A tidy ending, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like 'naturally' but means 'of a racecourse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits served undiluted, and the last level stretch of a racetrack before the finish.

clue.text: Small task force is only part of the picture

definitions.meaning: a detachment of soldiers given a particular job

definitions.text: is only part of the picture
definitions.meaning: a small item or feature within a larger whole

explanation.surface: A small unit's work is just one piece of the overall operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A military detachment, and a minor item or particular forming one feature of the whole.

clue.text: First half of one's performance switched in city

indicators.note: only the first two of the four letters are affected
switched means those letters trade places

parts.note: a solo is a performance by one person

explanation.surface: Half of a lone performance was rearranged in town.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Norway.

clue.text: Actor's entrance

parts.note: not an actor coming on stage, but the doorway at the back of a theatre used by performers

explanation.definitionFit: The theatre door used by performers and staff, reading 'entrance' as a way in rather than an arrival on stage.

clue.text: No Christian could be acting so badly

indicators.note: the words are performed badly, coming out in a muddled order

explanation.surface: No true Christian would behave so poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that God's existence cannot be known, and so is not a believing Christian.

clue.text: Thus Albert's left paper — editor stayed

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: Albert has left, so his short name departs from the paper

parts.note: a journal is a newspaper
Al is short for Albert

explanation.surface: So Albert quit the newspaper, but the editor remained.
explanation.definitionFit: To sojourn is to stay somewhere temporarily.

clue.text: Knew old-fashioned song could be a bloomer

parts.note: wist is an archaic past tense of wit, to know
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: An old tune turns out to be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant with purple flower clusters, so literally something that blooms.

clue.text: Violinist at home in an interval? Just the reverse

indicators.note: the whole phrase is to be read the other way round

parts.note: in means at home
an indefinite article giving A
a gap is an interval

explanation.surface: Was the violinist at home during the interval, or the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home in an interval' gives IN IN A GAP; 'Just the reverse' turns all of it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolo Paganini was the celebrated Italian virtuoso violinist.

clue.text: Roo's delight about Eeyore's tail

indicators.note: the word for delight goes about, that is around, the letter

parts.note: joy is delight

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: In Winnie-the-Pooh, little Roo is delighted with Eeyore's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Roo and Eeyore are characters in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh; Eeyore loses his tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A young kangaroo is called a joey, and Roo in the Pooh stories is one.

clue.text: Remove half a brace of ducks from vehicle, leaving this one

indicators.note: the instruction to remove means taking the letter out of the vehicle

parts.note: a scooter is a small vehicle
a duck is O (nought in cricket); a brace is two, so half is one O

explanation.surface: Take one of two ducks off a cart, and this is what is left.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of nought, written O; a brace of ducks is OO, and half is one O.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoter is a dark sea duck, so the duck left is one of the ducks the clue mentions.

clue.text: Expend on law makes Gray, for one, lose his head

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for Gray is cut off

parts.note: Thomas Gray wrote Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, so he was a writer of elegies

explanation.surface: A legal scholar sends the poet Gray out of his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray, the 18th-century English poet, is best known for his Elegy.
explanation.definitionFit: A legist is a specialist in law, especially Roman or civil law.

clue.text: Relative gain achieved by union

parts.note: the union is a marriage, and the gain is a new family member acquired through it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gain' and 'union' suggest trade unions and pay rises, but the union is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation by marriage, such as a spouse's parent.

clue.text: Soundly criticize performance of Chopin piece

indicators.note: soundly means the words are judged by how they are heard

parts.note: to knock is to criticize and a turn is a performance

explanation.surface: Thoroughly tear apart a performance of one of Chopin's works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but tells you to say KNOCK TURN out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopin wrote twenty-one nocturnes, dreamy night pieces for piano.

clue.text: Catches — very hard, they are

definitions.meaning: to nail a suspect is to catch or arrest them

explanation.surface: Grabs that are extremely tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally to catch someone out, and the metal spikes proverbial for toughness in hard as nails.

clue.text: Take over vessel

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the bowler takes an over of six deliveries

explanation.surface: Seize control of the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take over' reads as seize control, but in cricket an over is a set of six balls a bowler delivers.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver an over in cricket, and a round deep dish.

clue.text: True state briefly is seen in old game

parts.note: real means true
Tenn. is the abbreviation for Tennessee

explanation.surface: A frank account of the nation appears in a traditional sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The original indoor form of the racket sport, played in walled courts since the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Disadvantage for ward

parts.note: the clue word ward is what you get when the word draw is read back to front

explanation.walkthrough: 'For' links the definition to a reverse clue: draw read back gives ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a hindrance or downside.

clue.text: Part of salad served in Burlington House?

parts.note: home of the Royal Academy, RA
to dish is to serve food

explanation.surface: A salad ingredient is offered at a London gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House in Piccadilly, London, houses the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp red root vegetable eaten raw in salads.
